info.name: ELMS - Employee Leave Management System
info.description:
End-to-end test collection for the ELMS backend (6 services). Run as a Collection so requests flow in order: Auth populates tokens, Apply Leave populates request IDs, then Approve/Reject/Cancel exercise the lifecycle. All requests target the API Gateway at {{baseUrl}}.

Prerequisites: docker-compose up --build, all 8 containers healthy.

Seed identities (see shared/seed_config.py):
- manager1 / Manager@123  (id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001)
- emp1     / Employee@123 (id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002, reports to manager1)
- emp2     / Employee@123 (id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003, reports to manager1)

exec: // Compute date variables relative to today (UTC) so success/overlap/past-date
// scenarios are stable no matter when the collection is run.
// Range A: 3 days CASUAL for emp1 (success + overlap tests).
// Range B: 2 days PRIVILEGE for emp1 (reject test).
// Range C: 1 day SICK for emp1 (cancel test).
// Range D: 11 days SICK (insufficient-balance test, since SICK total = 10).
// Range E: 1 day used for the manager-id mismatch and circuit-breaker tests.

item.name: 01 - Authentication
item.description: POST /auth/login is the only public endpoint. Returns an HS256 JWT carrying sub (user id) and role. Bad creds and unknown users both return 401 with the same generic message (so the API does not leak which accounts exist).

item.name: 02 - Leave Balance
item.description: GET /employees/me/balances returns the caller's own balances. GET /employees/{id}/balances enforces RBAC: an employee may read only their own; a manager may additionally read direct reports. Each seeded employee starts with CASUAL=12, SICK=10, PRIVILEGE=15.

03 - Apply Leave
item.description: POST /leaves runs the four business validations in order: (1) start_date <= end_date - 400, (2) start_date >= today - 400, (3) number_of_days == inclusive day count - 400, (4) no overlap with existing PENDING/APPROVED requests - 409. After they pass, the service calls Leave Balance over httpx and returns 409 if balance is insufficient. Pydantic returns 422 for structural problems (missing/wrong-typed fields, days <= 0).

exec: pm.test('Status is PENDING and routed to manager1', function () {
pm.test('400 Bad Request (start > end)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });
pm.test('400 Bad Request (past date)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });
pm.test('400 Bad Request (day count mismatch)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });
pm.test('400 Bad Request (manager mismatch)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });

item.description: GET /leaves/history is the caller's own history with optional ?status filter (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED/ALL) and page/page_size pagination. Invalid status values return 400.

item.description: GET /manager/requests is manager-only (require_manager dependency returns 403 for employees). Results are scoped to the calling manager's team and support optional status / employee_id / from_date / to_date filters.

item.name: 06 - Manager: Approve
item.description: Approving a PENDING request orchestrates two downstream calls: (1) deduct days from the employee's balance via the Leave Balance Service, then (2) flip the request to APPROVED on the Leave Request Service. Both calls are wrapped in pybreaker circuit breakers.

exec: pm.test('409 Conflict (only PENDING requests can be approved)', function () {

item.name: 07 - Manager: Reject
item.description: Rejecting a PENDING request requires a non-empty rejection_reason (Pydantic min_length=1). Already-decided requests return 409. This folder first creates a fresh PENDING request to reject.

pm.test('409 Conflict (only PENDING can be rejected)', function () {

item.name: 08 - Cancel Leave
item.description: PATCH /leaves/{id}/cancel lets the owner cancel their PENDING request. 404 for unknown ids, 403 for someone else's request, 409 if the request is no longer PENDING.

request.description:
MANUAL test. Stop the leave-balance-service container, then send this request 5+ times in quick succession. The first few requests fail with 503 from the apply_leave endpoint catching httpx.HTTPError; once the breaker trips (failure threshold = 3), subsequent requests short-circuit with the same 503 but log 'Balance lookup circuit open'.

Steps:
  1) docker-compose stop leave-balance-service
  2) Send this request several times until the breaker opens
  3) docker-compose logs leave-request-service | grep 'circuit'
  4) docker-compose start leave-balance-service

exec: pm.test('503 Service Unavailable when balance service is down', function () {

request.description:
MANUAL verification. The OpenTelemetry SDK in shared/tracing.py exports spans via the ConsoleSpanExporter to each service's stdout. After running this request:

  docker-compose logs api-gateway leave-request-service | grep -i span

You should see correlated spans (api-gateway -> leave-request-service) carrying the trace_id from the traceparent header above.

MANUAL verification. The global exception handler in shared/exception_handlers.py publishes a SYSTEM_ERROR event to RabbitMQ whenever an unhandled exception escapes a route. The Notification Service consumer logs:

  [NOTIFICATION] SYSTEM_ERROR: <service>/<route> -> <message>

To trigger one: temporarily raise an unexpected exception in any route, hit it via this collection, and observe:

  docker-compose logs notification-service | grep SYSTEM_ERROR

The event payload mirrors the published JSON in shared/rabbitmq_publisher.py.
